CITY OF SIGNAL HILL
  2175 Cherry Avenue • Signal Hill, California 90755-3799

  THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL
  WELCOMES YOU TO A REGULAR
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  February 13, 2024

The City of Signal Hill appreciates your attendance. Citizen interest provides the Council and
Agency with valuable information regarding issues of the community. Meetings are held on
the 2nd and 4th Tuesday of every month.

Meetings begin at 6:00 pm with the conduct of any business permitted to be conducted in
closed session by the Brown Act (Government Code Section 54950, et seq.), if any, and with
the public portion of the meeting beginning at 7:00 pm. There is a period for public comment
on closed session matters at 6:00 pm prior to the closed session. In the event there is no
business to be conducted in closed session, the regular meeting shall begin at 7:00 pm.
There is a public comment period at the beginning of the regular meeting. Any person
wishing to comment shall be allotted three minutes per distinct item. Any meeting may be
adjourned to a time and place stated in the order of adjournment.

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting on the City’s website and outside of City
Hall. The agenda and related reports are also available for review online at
www.cityofsignalhill.org.

To view the meeting live at 7:00 p.m.:

  • City of Signal Hill website at www.cityofsignalhill.org, select the City Council
  Meetings Link from the home page.
  • Charter Spectrum Channel 3 or Frontier FiOS Channel 38.
To participate (closed session at 6:00 p.m. and regular meeting at 7:00 p.m.):

  • In-person Participation: Council Chamber of City Hall, 2175 Cherry Avenue, Signal
  Hill, California.
  • To make a general public comment or comment on a specific agenda item, you may
  also submit your comment, limited to 250 words or less, to the City Clerk at
  cityclerk@cityofsignalhill.org not later than 5:00 p.m. on Tuesday, February 13, 2024.
  Written comments will be provided electronically to City Council and attached to the
  meeting minutes. Written comments will not be read into the record.

(13)  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  a.  PUBLIC HEARING - A RESOLUTION AMENDING RESOLUTION NO.
  2023-06-6743, AMENDING THE UNIFORM SCHEDULE OF SERVICE FEES
  AND CHARGES

  Summary:

  Notice was published in the Signal Tribune newspaper per Government Code
  Section 65091(a) (4) on January 26 and February 2, 2024; and posted the
  notice in accordance with Signal Hill Municipal Code Section 1.08.010 on
  January 26, 2024.

  Consistent with State law, the City adopts a resolution approving adjustments to
  its Schedule of Fees and Charges, based on annual changes in the Consumer
  Price Index (CPI). On December 12, 2023, the City adopted Ordinance No.
  2023-11-1545, resulting in amendments and additions to the Signal Hill
  Municipal Code. With the adoption of Ordinance No. 2023-11-1545, the City
  Council approved new applications pertaining to filming activities, code
  enforcement, vending regulations, and other areas of health and safety. The
  City expects to receive applications related to these recent code updates; the
  proposed amendment to the City’s fee schedule would ensure the City recovers
  the cost associated with providing these services.

  Subject to City Council approval, and as provided for under State law, cities may
  collect user fees to recover costs incurred in providing a specific discretionary
  service. Pursuant to Government Code Section 660016, et seq., the specific
  fees to be charged for services must be adopted by the City Council by
  resolution, and upon approval would need to be incorporated into the Schedule
  of Fees and Charges.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 1  Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience.

  Goal No. 3  Economic & Downtown Development: Improve the local economy,
  support local businesses, and create a vibrant downtown core.

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure: Maintain and improve the City’s physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.
  Recommendations:

  1. Staff recommends the City Council open a public hearing, consider public
  testimony, approve the proposed service fees and charges.

  Page 3 of 9
 City Council  Regular  February 13, 2024

  2. Adopt the resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING RESOLUTION NO. 2023-06-6743, AMENDING THE
  UNIFORM SCHEDULE OF SERVICE FEES AND CHARGES
(14)  CITY MANAGER REPORTS

CALL THE HOUSING AUTHORITY TO ORDER

ROLL CALL

  CHAIR WOODS
  VICE CHAIR WILSON
  MEMBER COPELAND
  MEMBER HANSEN
  MEMBER JONES
  a.  EXCLUSIVE NEGOTIATION AGREEMENT (ENA)  WITH  NATIONAL
  COMMUNITY RENAISSANCE (NATIONAL CORE)

  Summary:

  In October 2023, the City Council and Housing Authority Board selected
  National Community Renaissance (National Core) as the preferred developer
  partner for the Orange Bluff and Walnut Bluff workforce housing sites. As a
  component of the selection process, the City Council directed staff to negotiate
  an Exclusive Negotiation Agreement (ENA). Over the past few months, staff
  worked with all parties to negotiate the terms, conditions, and project milestones
  of the ENA (Attachment A). The ENA is a contract that sets aside funds
  proposed as part of the City’s Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) specifically
  for National CORE in conjunction with the proposed workforce housing projects.
  The ENA prescribes a specific timeframe for National CORE to complete various
  performance requirements that, if achieved, would result in the City and National
  CORE negotiating an affordable housing agreement (“AHA”). Staff recommends
  the City Council and Housing Authority Board approve the ENA between the City
  of Signal Hill and National Community Renaissance substantially in the form
  presented for the development of the Orange Bluff and Walnut Bluff sites.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 1  Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience.

  Goal No. 3  Economic Development: Improve the local economy, support local
  businesses, and create a vibrant downtown core.

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure: Maintain and Improve the City’s physical
  infrastructure, waste system, and recreational spaces.
  Page 4 of 9
 City Council  Regular  February 13, 2024

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends the City Council and Housing Authority Board approve the
  Exclusive Negotiation Agreement (ENA) between the City of Signal Hill, the
  Signal Hill Housing Authority, and National Community Renaissance (“National
  CORE”) substantially in the form presented for the development of two proposed
  workforce housing projects known as Orange Bluff and Walnut Bluff.
RECESS THE HOUSING AUTHORITY

  b.  GENERAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH GRACE ENVIRONMENTAL
  INCORPORATED FOR VALVE EXERCISING SERVICES

  Summary:

  The City Council will consider entering into a three-year General Services
  Agreement with Grace Environmental Incorporated (GEI) for a not-to-exceed
  amount of $220,035. The scope of work includes exercising 1,597 valves
  located within the City’s water pipeline network, conducting a thorough condition
  assessment, and executing the associated flushing of pipeline segments. The
  proposed contract would provide the City with the ability to regularly exercise
  valve infrastructure, which is an industry best practice to maintain high water
  quality standards and reduce emergency maintenance related to leaks.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure: Maintain and improve the City’s physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.
  Recommendation:

  Authorize the City Manager to enter into a General Services Agreement with GEI
  for a three-year term contract for a not-to-exceed amount of $220,035, in a form
  approved by the City Attorney. This agreement encompasses the
  comprehensive exercising of all 1,597 valves within the City’s water pipeline
  network, conducting a thorough condition assessment, and performing the
  associated flushing of pipeline segments.
  c.  AGREEMENTS WITH BLUESPACE INTERIORS, LLC., AND MOHAWK
  COMMERCIAL, INCORPORATED FOR THE PURCHASE AND INSTALLATION
  OF CITY HALL FURNITURE, ARCHITECTURAL WALLS, AND FLOORING

  Summary:

  The recent public outreach effort associated with the Civic Center Master Plan
  found that the community desires to preserve City Hall as a place to conduct
  City business, a community gathering place, and a landmark. While the City has
  maximized the use of City Hall over the past few decades, certain elements
  have suffered from deferred maintenance. One of the key goals of the City Hall
  Renovation project is to significantly enhance the long-term viability of the
  Page 5 of 9
 City Council  Regular  February 13, 2024

  building so it may continue serving the public for many years. The City Council
  recently approved a renovation budget for City Hall that will provide for the
  replacement of office furnishings, replace flooring, make various repairs, and
  create more usable space. To advance this project, staff recommends approval
  of agreements with Bluespace Interiors, LLC. (Bluespace) and Mohawk
  Commercial, Incorporated (Mohawk) for the purchase and installation of new
  furniture, construction of architectural walls, and installation of flooring for City
  Hall, in a combined amount not-to-exceed $673,479.04. The proposed
  improvements would create 10 additional workstations and add a conference
  room to the ground floor of City Hall. Subject to City Council approval, the new
  furniture and flooring installation would begin by fall 2024 and be completed by
  early 2025.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 1  Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience.

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure: Maintain and improve the City’s physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.
  Goal No. 5  High-Functioning Government: Strengthen internal communication,
  recruitment, retention, system, and processes to increase the
  effectiveness and efficiency of City services.
  Recommendations:

  Staff is recommending approval of agreements with:

  1) Bluespace Interiors, LLC., for the purchase and installation of new
  furniture and architectural walls for City Hall, in an amount not to-exceed
  $529,474.37, in a form approved by the City Attorney, and authorize the
  City Manager to utilize a project contingency of up to 10% ($52,947.43) in
  the event of changed or unforeseen conditions, for a total budget of
  $582,421.80; and

  2) Mohawk Commercial, Incorporated for the purchase and installation of
  new flooring for City Hall, in an amount not to-exceed $144,004.67, in a
  form approved by the City Attorney; and authorize the City Manager to
  utilize a project contingency of up to 10% ($14,400.46) in the event of
  changed or unforeseen conditions, for a total budget of $158,405.13.
  d.  ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION RATIFYING THE CITY MANAGER’S
  PROCLAMATION OF THE EXISTENCE OF A LOCAL EMERGENCY IN
  RESPONSE TO 2024 FEBRUARY WINTER STORMS AND AUTHORIZING
  APPROPRIATIONS FROM THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-24 GENERAL FUND
  UNASSIGNED FUND BALANCE FOR IMMEDIATE SHORT-TERM REPAIRS

  Summary:

  Page 6 of 9
 City Council  Regular  February 13, 2024

  On February 4, 2024, Governor Gavin Newsom proclaimed a State of
  Emergency for eight counties in Southern California, including Los Angeles
  County, as a series of winter storms began impacting much of the State with
  high winds, damaging rain, and heavy snowfall. As of February 6, 2024, the City
  of Signal Hill experienced significant damage to the Panorama Promenade and
  Molino Avenue and 20th Street. California Government Code 8630, et. Seq.,
  and Signal Hill Municipal Code, Chapter 2, Section 2.76.060, provide the City
  Manager, as Director of Emergency Services, the authority to proclaim the
  existence of a local emergency if the City Council is not in session, which must
  be proclaimed within 10 days of an event. The City Council will consider
  adopting a resolution ratifying the proclamation of the existence of a local
  emergency in response to the February 2024 winter storms, made by the City
  Manager as the Director of Emergency Services, on February 7, 2024. The City
  Council will also consider adopting a proposed Resolution authorizing
  appropriations from the Fiscal Year 2023-24 General Fund Unassigned Fund
  Balance/Capital Improvement Projects Reserve fund for needed immediate
  short-term repairs in the amount of $800,000.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 1  Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience.

  Goal No. 2  Community Safety: Maintain community safety by supporting
  public safety services and increasing emergency preparedness.

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure: Maintain and improve the City’s physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.
  Recommendations:

  1. Adopt the resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA, RATIFYING THE PROCLAMATION OF THE EXISTENCE OF A
  LOCAL EMERGENCY BY THE CITY MANAGER OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL
  HILL, AS DIRECTOR OF EMERGENCY SERVICES

  2. Adopt the resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE ADOPTED BUDGET AND AUTHORIZING
  BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023-24 FOR THE
  EMERGENCY REPAIRS RESULTING FROM THE 2024 WINTER STORM
  DAMAGE IN THE AMOUNT OF $800,000.

  Page 7 of 9
 City Council  Regular  February 13, 2024

  COUNCIL MEMBER JONES

  VICE MAYOR WILSON
  MAYOR WOODS
(17)  ADJOURNMENT

  Tonight’s meeting will be adjourned to the next regular meeting of the Signal Hill City
  Council to be held on Tuesday, February 27, 2024, at 7:00 p.m., in the Council
  Chamber of City Hall, 2175 Cherry Avenue, Signal Hill, CA 90755.
CITIZEN PARTICIPATION

  Routine matters are handled most quickly and efficiently if contact is made with the City
  department directly concerned. However, if you would like to request that a matter be
  presented for City Council consideration, you may do so by writing to the City Council,
  City Clerk, or City Manager. The deadline for agenda items is 12 noon on the Tuesday

  Page 8 of 9
 City Council  Regular  February 13, 2024

  preceding the Council and Agency meetings. The complete agenda, including back up
  materials is available on the City website on the Friday preceding the meeting.

  If you need special assistance beyond what is normally provided to participate in City
  meetings, the City will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner.
  Please call the City Clerk's office at (562) 989-7305 at least 48 hours prior to the
  meeting to inform us of your particular needs and to determine if accommodation is
  feasible.

The City of Signal Hill appreciates your attendance. Citizen interest provides the Council and Agency with valuable information regarding issues of the community.  Meetings are held on the 2nd and 4th Tuesday of every month. 

Meetings begin at 6:00 pm with the conduct of any business permitted to be conducted in closed session by the Brown Act (Government Code Section 54950, et seq.), if any, and with the public portion of the meeting beginning at 7:00 pm. There is a period for public comment on closed session matters at 6:00 pm prior to the closed session. In the event there is no business to be conducted in closed session, the regular meeting shall begin at 7:00 pm. There is a public comment period at the beginning of the regular meeting.
